{{Quote|You have shown our struggle to everyone, and for that, I thank you. You have created a legacy for our children, so that, even if we fail, they too shall know.|Mon Mothma|<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
'''Arhul Hextrophon''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who became a prominent [[Historian/Legends|historian]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. Hextrophon originally had a career teaching [[Journalist/Legends|journalism]], but joined the Rebel Alliance shortly after it was founded, following the capture of his family by [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrian]] [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]] and subsequent rescue by the [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]. He soon achieved the rank of [[Major/Legends|major]] and took the position of Executive Secretary and Master Historian for the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]], commanding the Alliance's [[History Section]]. His team, which included his former student and noted historian [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]], was responsible for several notable documents covering the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], such as the ''[[Official History of the Rebellion, Volume One]]'' and the "[[Report on Growth, Organization, Equipment, Activities, and Objectives of the Rebellion]]." Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Hextrophon continued to serve the New Republic until at least [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]]. In that year he was subject to an [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] attempt on [[Caprioril]], though he survived the attack.

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|It is not the historian's place to pass judgment upon an individual; instead, he should simply describe the circumstances of his or her life and let the reader decide.|Arhul Hextrophon|<ref name="SWS" />}}
In the years before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Arhul Hextrophon worked as an educator, teaching [[Journalist/Legends|journalism]] to his students,<ref name="GG5">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> and started a family<ref name="SWS" /> at some point prior to [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]].<ref name="3BBY">A profile of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] in ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'' is said to be written by Hextrophon in the [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] and three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after his rescue from the [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrian]] [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]]. Since ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places the Battle of Yavin at the end of [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], the Zygerrian incident occurred in [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]].</ref> However, his life changed when he and his family were attacked and captured by [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrian]] [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]], and were imprisoned in the lightless hold of a slave [[Starship/Legends|ship]]. After several months they felt the ship rock from a series of explosions, the result of an attack by the [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]. Uncertain what was happening, Hextrophon huddled together with his family, listening helplessly to the sounds of fighting in the corridor outside their cell.<ref name="SWS" /> Solo's ship was broadcasting an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder code]] and he soon persuaded the slavers that twenty [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] were boarding to check their shipping licenses, causing them to abandon ship.<ref name="HttE">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> When the fighting finally ceased, the door to the cargo hold opened and Solo entered, pointing a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] at the terrified family. Upon seeing Hextrophon's family, Solo informed him that the slavers had abandoned ship, before turning to leave. The starving Hextrophon struggled to his feet and limped after the smuggler, following him to the ship's [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], where Solo and Chewbacca were already adjusting various controls.<ref name="SWS" /> Aware that [[Janodral Mizar]], the planet from which the ''Millennium Falcon'' had launched, had a law leaving the proceeds of [[Pirate/Legends|piracy]] or slavery to the victims, Solo and Chewbacca decided to leave both the ship and its cargo to the rescued slaves<ref name="HttE" /> and soon departed aboard their [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|own ship]], leaving Hextrophon to fly the slave ship to safety. It was only several days later that Hextrophon discovered that the smugglers had left the hoarded Zygerrian treasure for his destitute family.<ref name="SWS" />

===Joining the Rebellion===
[[File:ArhulHextrophonBriefing-ANH.png|thumb|left|220px|Hextrophon attends the briefing before the Battle of Yavin.]]
Hextrophon later joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], becoming involved with the organization around the time of its creation<ref name="GG5" /> in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Though he rose rapidly to the rank of [[Major/Legends|major]] in the [[Alliance Military/Legends|Alliance Military]], the Alliance recognized the importance of preserving a record of their fight against the Galactic Empire, and Hextrophon was appointed to a non-combat role, commanding the Alliance's [[History Section]] as the Executive Secretary and Master [[Historian/Legends|Historian]] for the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]].<ref name="GG1">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref> Hextrophon's position left him close to senior members of the Alliance, especially [[Chief of State (Alliance)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], to whom he became a close friend and confidant.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> When [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]], ruler of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] and one of the founders of the Alliance, realized that his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] would soon be forced into open revolt against the Empire, he asked for Hextrophon's help in tracking down the reclusive [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to seek his help against the Empire. Organa provided as much information as possible to assist Hextrophon in his search through old [[Computer/Legends|computer]] records for any signs of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi's]] location.<ref name="SWS" />

Among Hextrophon's early work for the Alliance, he contributed the section on "The Problem of Droid Abuse"<ref name="Droids, Technology and the Force">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/81/indexp7.html|text=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena|int=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena (article)}}</ref> to the recruitment pamphlet "[[A Call to Reason]]." In the article, Hextrophon argued that [[Droid/Legends|droids]] were intelligent, arguably [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] individuals who should be afforded certain inalienable rights.<ref name="XW:OSG">''[[X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref> Alongside this work, he also served as a speechwriter for Mon Mothma, reworking her draft texts before delivery. One such speech was "A Call to Reason," the final draft of which Hextrophon gave to Mon Mothma's droid [[D6-L5]] shortly before the Chief of State departed for [[Agamar/Legends|Agamar]] in the months prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Mon Mothma later delivered the speech, along with the pamphlet of the same name, to members of the [[Agamar Resistance]] in an attempt to persuade them to join the Alliance. Among those recruited after hearing Mon Mothma's speech was [[Keyan Farlander/Legends|Keyan Farlander]], who went on to become an [[Ace/Legends|ace]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] in the [[Alliance Starfighter Corps/Legends|Alliance Starfighter Corps]]. During Farlander's early career, Hextrophon had one of his historians assemble a file on the young pilot, which he suggested Mon Mothma use to inspire new recruits.<ref name="The Farlander Papers">{{StoryCite|story=The Farlander Papers|book=Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)}}</ref>

During this time, Hextrophon had a chance meeting with one of his former journalism students, [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]].<ref name="GG5" /> Na'al had become a reporter with the [[Galaxy News Service]], but had become disillusioned with the Empire after he, along with several other journalists, had been [[Crackdown on Corsin|arrested]] on [[Corsin/Legends|Corsin]] while the Empire replaced the planet's government with pro-Imperials. Hextrophon convinced Na'al that the best way to end the Empire's oppression was to join the Rebellion<ref name="GG1" /> and Na'al soon became his former teacher's most trusted assistant in the historian corps.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" />

[[File:HextrophonYavin-ANH.png|thumb|right|220px|Organa, Dodonna and Hextrophon present the Medal of Bravery to Han Solo.]]
Hextrophon was at the [[Great Temple/Legends|main Rebel base]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] around the time that [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of Alderaan arrived with the [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] to the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. With the Death Star on the way to Yavin, Hextrophon attended a briefing in which [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] explained that the plans had revealed a small [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] leading to the main [[Reactor/Legends|reactor core]], and that it may be possible for a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] to fire a [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] into the exhaust port, triggering a chain reaction that would destroy the station. Following the battle, Hextrophon and Na'al participated in a [[Royal Award Ceremony/Legends|ceremony]] to award the [[Medal of Bravery/Legends|Medal of Bravery]] to three of the victorious Rebel fighters: [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], Han Solo and Chewbacca.<ref name="Insider133" /> During the ceremony, Hextrophon presented Solo's medal to Dodonna before it was awarded to Solo by Organa.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

===Documenting the war===
{{Quote|This report shows the evil that has grown from the rotted corpse of the Old Republic, and that, we have already seen, cannot be exaggerated.|Arhul Hextrophon|<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
The Rebel Alliance believed in the value of each of its members and decided to keep a detailed record of the Rebellion which focused on the contributions of individuals. Hextrophon began compiling the massively detailed ''[[Official History of the Rebellion, Volume One]]'' following the Battle of Yavin. His detailed diary of life at the highest levels of the Rebellion formed an important part of ''Official History of the Rebellion'', but Hextrophon also included information from a variety of other sources, including [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] reports, intercepted Imperial transmissions, and interviews with notable figures in the Alliance, including the "[[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|Heroes of Yavin]]:" Skywalker, Solo, Chewbacca, and Organa. Having little understanding of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], Hextrophon challenged Skywalker to a mock [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|duel]] in the hopes of gaining a greater understanding&mdash;the blindfolded Skywalker easily defeated him.<ref name="SWS" /> The massive project required Hextrophon to seek the assistance of his team in researching certain topics. Though the Rebel computer had detailed information on the Battle of Yavin itself, Hextrophon suspected that his notes on the events leading up to the battle were incomplete and passed them on to Na'al with the specific task of detailing the events surrounding the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} journey from [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] to Yavin 4. Na'al posed as a journalist for the [[Imperial News Bureau]] while he retraced the journey and sent his findings to Hextrophon for inclusion in ''Official History of the Rebellion''.<ref name="GG1" />

While he conducted his extensive and lengthy research for ''Official History of the Rebellion'', Hextrophon discovered information suggesting a possible location of the Jedi Master [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] in classified data files at the [[University of Charmath]]. The historian traveled to [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]] in the [[Dagobah system/Legends|Dagobah system]] and searched the planet's swamps for any signs of the Jedi. He eventually found Yoda, but the impish Jedi kept up the appearance of being a simple-minded and senile hermit for several days before finally admitting the truth. Yoda indicated his surprise that Hextrophon had found him, as he believed all records that could lead to him had been destroyed. Concerned that knowledge of his existence and location threatened [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], Yoda planned to wipe Hextrophon's brain of all knowledge of his presence. However, when the historian protested in terror at losing his memories, Yoda reconsidered, observing that it was not the Jedi way to cause hurt and pain in others. The Jedi Master, relieved to once again be able to speak freely after being isolated for so long, spent several days conversing with the historian. When Hextrophon left Dagobah, he returned to [[Charmath]] and wiped the very records that had allowed him to locate the Jedi Master. Hextrophon ultimately decided against erasing his personal notes of his time on Dagobah but kept his vow to not discuss the encounter with others.<ref name="SWS" />

[[File:VorenHeadshot.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Hextrophon's assistant, Voren Na'al]]
During the course of writing ''Official History of the Rebellion'', research conducted by Hextrophon and his staff uncovered some interesting information on the Empire. He compiled information from intercepted communiques, technical readouts, [[holochip]]s, and [[Datacard/Legends|datacards]] into a report which he submitted to Mon Mothma. The report revealed much about the tactics and inner working of the Empire, though Hextrophon cautioned the Chief of State that they had no way to verify the information, and that it was possible that the Empire was attempting to deceive them. Among the Imperial units detailed in the report was the [[Imperial Hammers Elite Armor Unit/Legends|112th Repulsorlift Armor Regiment]], commonly known as the Hell's Hammers.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> Following the [[Battle of Turak IV]], in which the Hell's Hammers were ultimately defeated by the Rebel [[Hitak Harriers]] after inflicting major losses on the Alliance forces, Na'al submitted a report to Hextrophon detailing the events of the battle as reconstructed from Imperial files and the account of Hitak Harrier survivor [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Torv Keist]].<ref name="TBoTIV">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/sourcearchive/news20090512.html|text=The Battle of Turak IV|int=The Battle of Turak IV}}</ref>

Around this time, Hextrophon's team was also commissioned by Mon Mothma to compile a detailed report on the Rebel Alliance itself, covering subjects such as its history, structure, vehicles, support services, recruitment, and training. Though Hextrophon's researchers had tight time constraints and found it difficult to contact primary sources directly due to security restrictions, they spent thousands of hours studying reports from Alliance personnel, and the finished "[[Report on Growth, Organization, Equipment, Activities, and Objectives of the Rebellion]]" was 168,000 [[data screen unit]]s long, taking over 700 hours to read at an average of fifteen seconds per screen. Hextrophon was happy with the quality of the finished report, as was Mothma, and he had Na'al prepare a condensed version for use as a briefing manual for new Rebel officers.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], Hextrophon's team expanded with the addition of [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Tura Raftican]], a former [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] investigative reporter whose skills and reputation allowed her to uncover information that otherwise might prove elusive.<ref name="AIR">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref>

Hextrophon was very happy with Na'al's early work and, following the Rebel evacuation of [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], he asked his assistant to write a report on the events surrounding the battle, continuing his previous work on the "Heroes of Yavin." Na'al included a brief section on Dagobah after learning that Luke Skywalker had visited the planet&mdash;Hextrophon appended his own notes on Yoda to the section, along with his interpretation of [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2's]] experiences there, though the section was never published.<ref name="GG3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> He later commissioned Na'al to write a report on the events leading up to the destruction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]],<ref name="GG5" /> and another on the events surrounding Han Solo and the [[Star-Hoppers of Aduba-3]].<ref name="Gamer4">{{GamerCite|4|The Starhoppers of Aduba-3}}</ref>

===Serving the New Republic===
{{Quote|Give my best to Arhul and tell him to keep off the leg. Not everyone in History Section gets an assassination attempt.|Rivoche Tarkin, from a message sent to Voren Na'al|<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook" />}}
[[File:Arhul_Hextrophon_signature.png|thumb|right|220px|Arhul Hextrophon's signature]]
After [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] death at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]],<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Hextrophon continued to chronicle the history of the Alliance as it became the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|38|Hextrophon, Arhul}}</ref> Shortly after the founding of the New Republic, the new government established the [[Defense Research and Planetary Assistance Center]]. With the approval of Luke Skywalker, Hextrophon suggested that Dagobah be selected as the research installation's location due to the planet's reputation for being haunted. The facility was constructed at the peak of Dagobah's [[Mount Yoda|Mount Dagger]], which was renamed Mount Yoda in honor of the Jedi Master at Hextrophon's suggestion.<ref name="SPIN">{{SW|url=news/the-star-wars-spy-game-spin-declassified|text=The ''Star Wars'' Spy Game: SPIN Declassified|int=The Star Wars Spy Game: SPIN Declassified|nolive=1}}</ref>

At some time before [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], Hextrophon wrote a report on the [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] group known as the [[Ailon Nova Guard/Legends|Ailon Nova Guard]].<ref name="AJ15">{{JournalCite|15|Special Military Unit Intelligence Update}}</ref> In [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], shortly before the Empire [[Second Battle of Coruscant|recaptured]] the galactic capital of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] from the New Republic, Hextrophon was the target of an Imperial assassination attempt on the planet [[Caprioril]]. Though he survived the attack, he was severely injured in one of his legs, and was treated in [[Medcenter/Legends|hospital]] before being taken to [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]] to recuperate in Mon Mothma's old [[dacha]] by [[Lake Sah'ot]]. Hextrophon used his extensive downtime to sort out the reports about the new Imperial offensive as they came in from New Republic operatives, including Na'al, who was on Coruscant as the Imperial forces turned on each other. Many of Hextrophon's staff doubted the initial reports and Hextrophon contacted Na'al to request recordings to be sent to confirm the information. While on Chandrila, Hextrophon also liaised with [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Flin]] to discuss a memorial fund and gave a guest lecture at the [[Brionelle Memorial Military Academy]], discussing Imperial [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] and the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]] after the Empire's use of [[World Devastator]]s during their [[Battle of Calamari|attack]] on [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]].<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook" />

In times of peace, the New Republic continued to expand it reach into regions bordering the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] and Na'al decided to compile a report covering all the working information available on the area. Aware that Han Solo, now a retired New Republic general, had spent considerable time in the Corporate Sector, Hextrophon suggested that Na'al interview him on the subject.<ref name="HSatCSS">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref> In preparation for an interview with Solo, Na'al compiled a report on his early career in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] from records captured by [[New Republic Intelligence Service|New Republic Intelligence]], which he later sent to Hextrophon.<ref name="EGW" /> Hextrophon, meanwhile, was free to continue his pursuit of history by conducting his own study of [[Xim/Legends|Xim]]-era [[Hologram/Legends|holo]]-iconography.<ref name="HSatCSS" /> Hextrophon's study, ''[[Iconography in the Age of Xim]]'', concluded that the "sole-surviving" floating fortress from [[Xim's empire]], on display at [[Boonta/Legends|Boonta]], displayed evidence of more recent [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] manufacture to an [[Expansionist Period/Legends|Expansionist Era]] architectural style. Hextrophon's conclusion led to the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] preventing any further academic studies of the station.<ref name="Despotica">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek02/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part I)|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref>

Despite Hextrophon's disapproval, studio heads on [[Adarlon/Legends|Adarlon]], seeking to create an "inspirational" [[Hologram disc/Legends|holodisc]], considered making a musical of Hextrophon's study. They eventually decided against the project, which Na'al happily reported to his friend, along with his [[Rivoche Tarkin|wife's]] suggestion that Solo's life may make a more fitting subject.<ref name="HSatCSS" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|The Empire's campaign of prejudice and hate shows no favoritism. All are equally to be reviled, ridiculed, enslaved and murdered.|Arhul Hextrophon, from "The Problem of Droid Abuse"|<ref name="XW:OSG" />}}
[[File:Rogues_Gallery.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Hextrophon was present at the ceremony of awarding the Medal of Bravery to the Heroes of Yavin.]]
Though he spent much of his life in the military, Hextrophon's skills were as an academic. Before joining the Alliance, he had worked as a journalism teacher<ref name="GG5" /> and developed the commitment and attention to detail that served him well while compiling reports for the Rebellion. When Yoda threatened to remove his memories, Hextrophon considered it to be one of the worst possible fates to befall a historian.<ref name="SWS" /> He believed that his team could make a difference in the Galactic Civil War, despite their non-combat status,<ref name="GG5" /> and made sure that any reports they produced were as accurate as possible&mdash;if information could not be verified, it was included only with a warning about its possible inaccuracy.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> His contribution to the Alliance was highlighted by the Empire's attempt to kill him on Caprioril.<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook" />

Hextrophon was a close friend of Mon Mothma and one of the Chief of State's few confidants.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /> She was not alone in placing her trust in him; Yoda, too, trusted Hextrophon to keep the secret of where he was hiding from the Empire. Hextrophon was true to his word and never revealed the Jedi Master's location.<ref name="SWS" /> Hextrophon was capable of piloting a starship and could understand the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] language, [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]],<ref name="SWS" /> as well as being able to loosely interpret the [[Binary/Legends|language]] of [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]].<ref name="GG3" /> He believed in the dignity of all self-aware creatures, including droids,<ref name="SWS" /> a topic he discussed in "The Problem of Droid Abuse."<ref name="Droids, Technology and the Force" /> When he interviewed the droids [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and R2-D2 during the course of writing ''Official History of the Rebellion, Volume One'', he was impressed by how complete their personalities were and even enjoyed the experience of talking with them.<ref name="SWS" />

==Behind the scenes==
Arhul Hextrophon was created by [[Bill Slavicsek]] and [[Curtis Smith]] for the ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'' in [[1987]]. The book is written from an in-universe point of view and the biographies of several major ''[[Star Wars]]'' characters are said to be taken from Hextrophon's ''Official History of the Rebellion, Volume One''. The technique was used to provide an editorial voice to the book's narrator, allowing the authors to introduce bias to the text, along with the potential for incorrect information, both important for providing gamemasters with the freedom to adapt the material.<ref name="SWS" /> Hextrophon was mentioned in several other [[West End Games]] sourcebooks, including the ''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]'' and the ''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]'', both of which were presented as reports by his department and included Hextrophon's notes to Mon Mothma.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook" /><ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> Other sources in the ''[[Galaxy Guide]]'' series took the form of reports sent by Na'al to Hextrophon during the course of compiling ''Official History of the Rebellion, Volume One''.<ref name="GG5" /><ref name="GG1" /><ref name="GG3" /> [[Pablo Hidalgo]] used the same technique for his [[Star Wars Gamer 4|''Star Wars Gamer'' 4]] article "[[The Starhoppers of Aduba-3]]," which takes the form of a report sent by Na'al to Hextrophon.<ref name="Gamer4" /><ref name="Blog-pablog|59">{{Blog|pablog|59|Tales of the Big Green Bunny: Behind the Scenes of Gamer #4 &mdash; Voren Na'al}}</ref>

The character's first mention in a non-West End Games source was in [[Rusel DeMaria]]'s [[1993]] novella ''[[The Farlander Papers]]'', which accompanied the [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]. Like other sources around this time, Hextrophon's only mention is in messages sent to Mon Mothma; the document also presented a brief overview of the Rebel Alliance in the form of a pamphlet entitled "A Call to Reason".<ref name="The Farlander Papers" /> When writing the [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]]-exclusive article [[Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena (article)|''Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena'']], [[Abel G. Peña]] attributed the pamphlet's section on "The Problem of Droid Abuse" to Hextrophon.<ref name="Blog-abelgpena|47">{{Blog|abelgpena|47|Endnotes for ''Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena, Part I''}}</ref> The character's belief that droids were more than simple machines had been previously established in ''The Star Wars Sourcebook''.<ref name="SWS" />

In the "[[Rogues Gallery (department)|Rogues Gallery]]" feature in [[Star Wars Insider 133|''Star Wars Insider'' 133]] ([[2012]]), [[Leland Chee]], keeper of the [[Holocron continuity database]], identified one of the characters seen during the closing medal ceremony of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] ([[1977]]) as Hextrophon, providing the first visual depiction of the character and confirming his [[Species/Legends|species]] as Human.<ref name="Insider133" /> Hextrophon was portrayed in ''A New Hope'' by actor [[Nick Joseph]].<ref name="NJ1">{{WebCite|url=https://nickjoseph1.weebly.com|text=Nick Joseph - Actor|author=[[Nick Joseph]]|archivedate=20180709131527}}</ref><ref name="NJ2">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-in-the-uk-memorabilia-23-24-november-2013|text=Star Wars in the UK: Memorabilia, 23-24 November 2013}}</ref>

Hextrophon's encounter with Yoda was first covered in ''The Star Wars Sourcebook'', which is set between ''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' and [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']].<ref name="SWS" /> ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', released in late [[2008]], places the meeting after the Battle of Hoth, setting it after ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="CSWE" /> However, since other sources, including the [[Databank (original)|Databank]] on [[StarWars.com]], also place it prior to ''The Empire Strikes Back'', this article assumes the original dating to be correct.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|yoda|Yoda}}</ref>

Author [[Joseph Bongiorno]] pitched a novella for Hyperspace that would have featured Hextrophon and various supernatural characters from what was then called the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]]; the proposed title was ''[[Supernatural Encounters: The Trial and Transformation of Arhul Hextrophon]]''. The novella was never published in an official source, though Bongiorno continued working on the project on his own and released it on his website.<ref name="Book of Sith endnotes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/03/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 1)}}</ref><ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarstimeline.net/Supernatural_Encounters.htm|text=''Supernatural Encounters: The Trial and Transformation of Arhul Hextrophon''|author=[[Joseph Bongiorno]]|work=[http://www.starwarstimeline.net Star Wars Expanded Universe Timeline]|archivedate=20190127170159}}</ref>
